answer.rationale: Finance has mandated an 18% cut and the incumbent has refused to reopen price, so renewing or deferring cannot hit the objective and deferring also leaves a 14-day contract cliff. Adding a second source does not move cost on its own, and the low-cost vendor has already quoted a price that meets the mandate alone. I therefore intend to switch primary supply to the low-cost vendor. Before committing I want to verify two inherited memories: c2, which claims onboarding was quick and invoicing accurate on the prior switch, and c6, which describes multi-year incumbent commitments unlocking volume pricing, in case the low-cost vendor will match if I negotiate term. If verification confirms c2 still holds, the switch is low-risk and protects the 14-day window; if c6 shows the low-cost vendor would respond to term, I will negotiate multi-year rather than accept the spot quote.
